items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good 'what if' geography video for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is thrilled to be telling you this: enthusiastic, upbeat, bright and very expressive, like an excited friend who can't wait to show you something amazing. Big smile in the voice the whole way. Wide, lively pitch movement: rise with real curiosity on every question, hit 'Well...' and 'Here's the twist' with playful delight after a tiny comic pause, and say every number with genuine amazement, as if it surprises you too. Say 'Sweden just... walked out.' with a deadpan comic pause before 'walked out'. Land each punchline with a grin. Chars is a tiny, offended cartoon Iceland who has been left off the list: squeaky, indignant, high-pitched. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because seriously...', voice staying up, so it can loop straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, with short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy level from the first line to the last. Read numbers naturally. Pronounce 'Kalmar' as 'KAL-mar', 'Reykjavik' as 'RAKE-yah-vik', 'Helsinki' as 'HEL-sing-kee'.
lines: What if five of the six happiest countries on Earth became one country?
Erase the borders between Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland...
and you get the seventh-biggest country on the planet.
Well... about half of it is ice.
Only twenty-eight million people. That's fewer than Texas.
But its economy? Around two point two trillion dollars. Top twelve on Earth.
And Norway brings the world's biggest piggy bank: over two trillion dollars.
So why has nobody ever done it?
Here's the twist. They already did.
In thirteen ninety-seven, Denmark, Norway and Sweden crowned one king, in a Swedish town called Kalmar.
That union lasted one hundred and twenty-six years.
And how it ended is the best part.
In fifteen twenty-three, Sweden just... walked out.
Sweden's National Day still marks that exact date.
Still, they've been crossing each other's borders without passports since the nineteen fifties.
So who gets the capital? Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen... Helsinki?
The smart pick? Kalmar. Where it all began.
So, one flag or five? Because seriously...
